send agents to use `nak req -k 1 -a fa984bd7dbb282f07e16e7ae87b26a2a7b9b90b7246a44771f0cf5ae58018f52 -outbox | jq -r .content` and to paginate to go through all my notes and to find content to include in my site and notes to embed statically in the site.
 [...] User: include the one that says "I'm so bullshit about nostr"
 [...] Assistant: You're right, that was wasteful — let me stop it and restructure as a two-stage pipeline: Sonnet does the cheap extraction pass over the 5600 notes, then Fable only sees the condensed distillate for the actual creative decisions.

User: [Request interrupted by user for tool use]

User: start building the schematics of the site with lorem ipsum and open it on my browser so I can give you feedback bro

User: even a haiku agent to remove the crap first would be better

User: or multiple haiku agents

User: to go through the 5600 -- remove the obvious bad ones [...] Assistant: Got it — building the visual skeleton first so you can react to layout, and I'll queue cheap Haiku agents to triage the 5600 notes in parallel rather than reading them wholesale.

Assistant: Now let's serve it and open in your browser.

Assistant: Site is live at http://localhost:8123/ with placeholder (lorem ipsum) copy for home, `/stuff/`, and `/nownownow/` — black on white, serif, no JS, no images, thin hairlines. It should have opened in your browser. Take a look and tell me what to change (fonts, spacing, layout, nav style, etc.) before I wire in real content.

Meanwhile, I'll spin up a batch of Haiku agents to triage the 5600 nostr notes into signal vs. noise, cheaply. [...] Assistant: All 10 triage chunks combined into one 3,116-line signal file (down from 5,612 raw notes). A Sonnet agent is now reading through it plus the repo timeline to build a dated "why"-focused briefing, going back to 2020 (with repo-creation dates extending context back to 2012). I'll let it run in the background and pick up with the Fable copywriting pass once it's done.
